column2: Manohar Lal Sharma v. Union of India
column12: Whether the Court should order an independent inquiry into alleged Pegasus spyware surveillance of citizens.
column13: A bare plea of national security did not shield the Union; an expert committee was appointed to inquire into the surveillance claims.
column14: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)

column2: X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Govt. of NCT of Delhi
column11: r 3B MTP Rules; s 3(2) MTP Act
column12: Whether unmarried women can terminate a 20–24 week pregnancy, and whether a doctor must reveal a minor's identity to police under POCSO.
column13: Unmarried women fall within the 20–24 week category; a doctor reporting under s 19 POCSO need not disclose the minor's identity.

column2: Aparna Ajinkya Firodia v. Ajinkya Arun Firodia
column12: Whether a family court can order a DNA test of a child to prove the wife's adultery.
column13: DNA tests of children cannot be ordered routinely; the child's privacy and legitimacy must be protected, so the order was set aside.
column14: Goutam Kundu v. State of West Bengal (1993)

column2: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India
column12: Whether donor informational privacy justifies anonymous political funding through electoral bonds.
column13: Voters' right to information outweighed donor privacy; the Electoral Bond Scheme was struck down.
column14: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)

column2: Frank Vitus v. Narcotics Control Bureau
column12: Whether bail can require the accused to share a Google Maps PIN location with the police.
column13: A bail condition letting police track every movement of the accused violates privacy; the PIN condition was deleted.
column14: State of A.P. v. Challa Ramkrishna Reddy (2000)

column2: In Re: Right to Privacy of Adolescents (with State of West Bengal v. Probhat Purkait)
column12: Whether a High Court could acquit a POCSO accused on the footing of a ‘consensual’ adolescent relationship and lecture adolescents on sexual conduct.
column13: The conviction was restored and the High Court's remarks set aside; a minor's consent is immaterial under POCSO.
column14: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012)

column2: Amlesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
column12: Whether a High Court could accept a police plan to narco-test all accused while hearing a bail plea.
column13: Forced narco tests are never permissible; a voluntary test may be sought only at the defence stage with court permission.

column12: Whether phone calls secretly recorded by one spouse are admissible in divorce proceedings.
column13: Such recordings are admissible; the wife's privacy objection did not bar them, and the Family Court's order was restored.
column14: R.M. Malkani v. State of Maharashtra (1973)

column11: Art 21; s 112 Evidence Act; ss 53, 53A CrPC
column12: Whether a man accused of cheating could be forced to give a DNA sample to establish a child's paternity.
column13: Forced DNA testing is a grave intrusion on privacy and must be lawful, necessary and proportionate, with a nexus to the offence. Paternity was collateral to the charges, so the direction was set aside.
column14: Goutam Kundu v. State of West Bengal (1993)

column2: Harish Rana v. Union of India
column12: How passive euthanasia applies to a patient in a permanent vegetative state who cannot consent and left no advance directive.
column13: Withdrawal of artificial nutrition was permitted through surrogate decision-making and medical boards.
column14: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018)

column3: 2026 INSC 600 (arising out of SLP (C) No. 4016 of 2026)
column12: Whether a man could be compelled to take a DNA test in a suit where the plaintiff claims to be his son.
column13: Privacy is not absolute; where paternity is directly in issue and no other evidence can settle it, a DNA test may be ordered. The Civil Court was directed to fix a date for the test.
column14: Aparna Ajinkya Firodia v. Ajinkya Arun Firodia (2023)
